A_target.statement:
Let $u, v \in \R^n$.
Then:
:$\size {u \cdot v} \le \norm u \norm v$
where $\cdot$ denotes the [[Definition:Dot Product|dot product]].

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a [[Definition:Real Inner Product Space|real inner product space]].
Then:
:$\forall u, v \in V: \size {\innerprod u v} \le \norm u \norm v$

validity_conditions: The dot product on R^n is a genuine inner product (bilinear, symmetric, positive-definite), so the abstract theorem applies directly.
No new argument is needed; this is instantiation, hence specialization.
proof_plan:
From the [[Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz Inequality/Inner Product Spaces|Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz Inequality]] for [[Definition:Real Inner Product Space|real inner product spaces]]:
:$\size {\innerprod u v} \le \norm u \norm v$

Let $V = \R^n$ with $\innerprod u v = u \cdot v$.
By [[Dot Product is Inner Product]], this is a real inner product space, with $\norm u = \sqrt {u \cdot u}$.
